newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine October inflation seen blipping up.
newsitem.headline: Argentine October inflation seen blipping up.

text.p: Argentine analysts said Friday they expect October consumer inflation, due out Monday, at 0.8 to 1.3 percent, up from 0.2 percent in September and 0.3 percent in October 1995.

"We calculate that it will jump to 1.3 percent, which would be the highest rise in prices since May 1993 and would take inflation over the past 12 months to 1.2 percent," said Nestor Touzet, of consultants Broda y Asociados.
"The rise is a result of a number of isolated factors such as hikes in transport and fuel prices and not of any structural return to monthly single-digit inflation," he said.
Gasoline prices rose by 14 percent in October, diesel rose by 46 percent and public transport by 10-25 percent.
The Macroeconomica consultancy thought higher fuel and transport prices would be partially offset by seasonal falls in fruit and vegetables. It forecast the month's overall inflation at 0.8 percent.
Jose Luis Espert, director of Econometrica, predicted 0.9 percent inflation. Both Banco Quilmes and C&E estimated prices would be up by 1.2 percent.
Annual inflation was 0.2 percent in September.
